questions.question: As per ’Basel III: A global regulatory framework for more resilient banks and banking systems’ released in December 2010, banks will be required to hold a capital conservation buffer of ______ of risk weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity to withstand future periods of stress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basel III** is a set of international banking regulations developed by the Bank for International Settlements in order to promote stability in the international financial system.
 
• The **Basel Committee** published the Basel III rules text in **December 2010.**
 
• It covers the worldwide regulatory criteria on bank capital adequacy and liquidity that were agreed upon by the Governors and Heads of Supervision and adopted by the** G20 Leaders** at their November summit in Seoul.
 
• To withstand future periods of stress, banks will be required to keep a capital conservation buffer of **2.5%**__ of risk-weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity under Basel III.
 
• The results of the Committee's complete **quantitative impact research** were also released (QIS).
 
• **Nout Wellink** was the Chairman of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
 
• Basel Committee on Banking Supervision examines and proposes ways to reconfigure global banking regulations.
 
• The Committee estimated that Group 1 banks in aggregate would have had a shortfall of €577 billion at the end of 2009.
 
• The Basel III accord increased the minimum Basel III capital requirements for banks from 2% in Basel II to 4.5% of common equity, as a percentage of the bank’s risk-weighted assets.
 
• In order to be Basel compliant, there is additionally a 2.5% buffer capital requirement, bringing the total minimum requirement to 7%.
 
• When banks are in financial distress, they can use the buffer, but doing so can result in even more financial constraints when it comes to paying dividends.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Indian National Congress and the ______.

__
 
• The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Congress and the Muslim League.
 
• Congress and the Muslim League decided to work together for **representative government in the country** through the Lucknow pact.
 
• As a result of the Lucknow Pact, congress accepted **separate electorates.**
 
• This was the first time both the INC and the Muslim League's leaders had met in a joint session.
 
• The pact provided a joint political platform for the** Moderates, Extremists, and the Muslim League.​**
 
• The Indian National Congress was headed by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and the All-India Muslim League was led by **Muhammad Ali Jinnah.**
 
• Lucknow Pact was adopted by Congress at its Lucknow session on **29 December 1916.**
 
• Lucknow Pact was adopted by the Muslim League on **31 December 1916.**
 
• The Pact addressed both the structure of India's government and the relationship between **Hindu and Muslim communities.**
 
• This Lucknow pact prepared the door for Hindu-Muslim cooperation in the **Khilafat movement**, as well as Mohandas Gandhi's **non-cooperation movement**, which began in 1920.
 
• Muslim League was formed in **1906.**

questions.question: Which form of farming is called ‘slash and burn’ agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Primitive subsistence farming.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slash-and-burn agriculture** is a type of farming in which forests are burned and cleared to make way for crops.
 
• Slash and burn agriculture is **primitive subsistence farming.**__
 
• The ‘slash and burn agriculture is known as **‘Milpa’** in Mexico and Central America.
 
• **Shifting cultivation** is also known as ‘slash and burn agriculture.
 
• The initial step in the technique is to clear an area of trees and woody plants.
 __
 
• The "slash," or felled vegetation, is then allowed to dry, usually just before the rainy season starts.
 
• The biomass is then burned, producing a nutrient-rich layer of ash that fertilises the soil while temporarily eliminating weed and pest species.
 
• Due to nutrient depletion and weed and pest invasion, the plot's output diminishes after three to five years, compelling the farmers to quit the field and shift to a new place.
 
• Due to a shortage of natural fertilisers and insecticides, among other things, productivity is low.
 
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture will lead to **deforestation.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8efaef53ff23a2b542c6377416fdb16f3da34c0c88e26fbd23d03f192d3905e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intensive subsistence agriculture** is a type of farming in which farmers cultivates a small plot of land using simple tools and more labour.
 
• **Commercial farming** is a kind of farming that employs bigger doses of contemporary inputs in order to increase output.
 
• **Hydroponic farming**, often known as soilless farming, is a method of growing plants without the use of soil.

questions.question: The Energy and Resources Institute and NDMA has launched a Flood Early Warning System (FEWS) for Guwahati to alert local authorities about flash floods or any heavy rainfall in August 2020. What is the full form of NDMA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Disaster Management Authority.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• The** Energy and Resources Institute(TERI)** and NDMA(**National Disaster Management Authority**__) launched a Flood Early Warning System (FEWS) to predict floods in Guwahati.
 
• The Flood Early Warning System (FEWS) will alert local authorities about** flash floods and/or heavy rainfall.**
 
• It was developed under TERI's project supported by the NDMA in collaboration with the** India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA).
 
• The system is developed with inbuilt urban drainage to predict flood at street-level accuracy.
 
• The flood level and hotspot locations can be shown using Google Maps, which will aid in the identification of flood-affected areas, disaster preparedness, and management of urban flooding-related concerns like traffic disruption, relief and recovery, and stormwater management.
 
• The fully automated system, which uses advanced hydrological models to provide warnings with a lead time of 72 hours, is replicable across India.
 
• This is in accordance with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent statement during a meeting with the Chief Ministers of six states—**Assam, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala**—discussing the importance of developing a local-level flood warning system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority**__

 
 
• **(NDMA)** is the **apex body for Disaster Management in India.**

 
 
• **The body is headed by the Prime Minister of India.**
 
• **State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs)** headed by respective Chief Ministers.
 
• The **Government of India passed the Disaster Management Act on December 23, 2005, which established the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA),**
 
 
 
 
 
• **The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI)** is a multi-faceted, independent organisation with research, policy, consulting, and implementation skills.

questions.solution:

• The **bicameral state legislature** has two houses to make a law namely legislative assemblies and legislative councils(Vidhan Parishad).

• States with Legislative Council are:
 __
 
• Andhra Pradesh
 
• Bihar
 
• Karnataka
 
• Maharashtra

• Union Territories like **Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry** have their own legislative assembly and council of ministers.
 
• **Vidhan Parishads** are also known as Legislative councils.
 
 
• Vidhan Parishads are the upper houses of the provincial legislature in the different states of India.
 
• Vidhan Parishad is analogous to **Rajya Sabha.**
 
• Members of the Vidhan Parishad are indirectly elected and nominated.
 
• The maximum strength of the Vidhan Parishad is fixed at o**ne-third of the total strength of the assembly.**

questions.question: JPEG is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images. What is the full form of JPEG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Joint Photographic Experts Group__**.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group**__.

 __
 
• It is a computer graphics file format.
 
• JPEG is a lossy compression method widely used for digital photographs.
 
• In JPEG, the image is compressed to make a smaller file.
 
• Compression results in a loss of quality, however, so it is usually undetectable.
 
• JPEG files are widely used on the Internet, and JPEG is a popular digital camera format, making it ideal for non-professional printing and web use.
 
• JPEG format is best for web images, non-professional printing, e-mail, PowerPoint.
 
• The extensions ".jpeg" and ".jpg" are used for JPEG files.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PNG** (Portable Network Graphics) files are a lossless picture format that was created to replace and improve upon the gif format.
 
• **GIF** files (Graphics Interchange Format) are used for web graphics and can be animated and transparent.
 
• **BMP **(Bitmap Image File) is a file format designed by Microsoft for Windows that does not compress or lose information, allowing images to have very high quality while simultaneously having very large file sizes.

questions.question: ______ is the process of allowing particles in suspension in water to settle out of the suspension under the effect of gravity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sedimentation**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__**Sedimentation is the process of allowing particles in suspension in water to settle out of the suspension under the effect of gravity**__.

__
 
• When the heavier component in a mixture settles after water is added to it, the process is called sedimentation.
 
• Under the Sedimentation process, all of the solids settle to the bottom of the beaker, leaving a clear layer of liquid on top.
 
• Sedimentation is a filtering procedure used in water treatment plants to remove undesirable particles from dirty water.
 
• Sedimentation also helps to determine the medical conditions of a person.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decantation** is the separation process in which two immiscible liquids are separated.

 
 
• When the water (along with the dust) is removed, the process is called decantation.
 
• Decantation is the process of separating a mixture of oil and water.
 
 
 
• **Filtration** can be used to separate components of a mixture of an insoluble solid and a liquid.
 
• The selective boiling and subsequent condensation of a component in a liquid combination are referred to as **distillation.**
